metaDescription: We evaluated six jobsite table saws on rip capacity, fence design, blade brake, stand and weight to help you rip sheet goods and lumber safely and accurately.
expertTake: The DEWALT DWE7491RS is our best overall pick because it pairs a 10 inch blade, a 32-1/2 inch rip capacity, a rack and pinion telescoping fence and a rolling stand in a package built around real jobsite use. The SKIL TS6307 is the value pick for a folding-stand 10 inch saw at a gentler tier. Anyone who works with a lot of hardwood or wants the safest possible machine should skip a portable saw and look at a cabinet or flesh-sensing model.
introParagraphs: A jobsite table saw is a portable, lightweight version of the shop table saw, built to rip lumber and plywood on site and fold into a truck or garage corner. It trades some mass and power for portability, but the best ones still cut accurately and safely.

Fence quality decides accuracy, the stand decides how steady the saw feels, and the guard and blade brake decide how safe it is. Rip capacity, blade size and motor power matter, but they are secondary to how well the saw holds its alignment.

products.name: DEWALT DWE7491RS 10 Inch Table Saw with Rolling Stand
products.description:
The DEWALT DWE7491RS is a 10 inch jobsite table saw with a 15 amp motor running at 4,800 RPM, a 32-1/2 inch rip capacity and a rack and pinion telescoping fence that adjusts quickly and stays parallel to the blade. It comes with a foldable rolling stand, and DEWALT lists a patented material support that helps with narrow rip cuts.

The tradeoff is size and weight. This is a bigger, heavier portable saw than the 8-1/4 inch compact models, so it is harder to carry up stairs, and the stand adds bulk. Compared with the DEWALT DWE7485, which has a 24.5 inch rip capacity, the 7491RS handles full 32-1/2 inch rips and uses a larger blade for deeper cuts. It suits remodelers, deck builders and serious home workshops.

Check blade parallelism to the miter slot before critical work, keep the rack and pinion clean, and replace the blade when it dulls. Use a push stick, never stand in line with the blade, and keep the guard and riving knife in place for through cuts.
products.bestFor: Remodelers and serious DIYers who need a full-size, portable rip saw.
pros: Thirty-two and a half inch rip capacity handles large sheet goods
Rack and pinion telescoping fence is fast and stays parallel
Included rolling stand moves easily around a site or garage
Ten inch blade gives deeper cuts than compact saws
cons: Heavier and bulkier than 8-1/4 inch compact saws
Stand takes space even when folded

products.name: BOSCH GTS15-10 10 Inch Jobsite Table Saw with Rise Stand

specList.label: Brake
specList.value: Convenience brake, stops blade in about three seconds

products.description:
The Bosch GTS15-10 is a 10 inch jobsite saw with a 15 amp motor at 3,800 RPM, a 32-1/8 inch rip capacity, a rack and pinion fence with colour-coded index pins and a convenience brake that, per the listing, stops the blade in about three seconds. It ships with the Rise wheeled stand that lets you set up and fold the saw quickly.

The tradeoff is that the motor speed is lower than the 4,800 RPM figures on some competitors, and the saw is large for a jobsite model. Compared with the DEWALT DWE7491RS, the Bosch adds a blade brake and a different stand design, but costs more and is not clearly faster in cutting. It suits users who value the brake and a stand that is easy to deploy.

Check the brake pad, keep the fence rails clean and align the blade to the miter slot. Use a push stick and keep the riving knife installed.
products.bestFor: Users who want a blade brake and a fast-deploying stand.
pros: Convenience brake stops the blade in about three seconds
Thirty-two and an eighth inch rip capacity handles sheet goods
Colour-coded index pins speed repeat fence settings
Rise stand sets up and folds quickly
cons: Lower RPM figure than some competing 15 amp saws
Larger and costlier than basic jobsite saws

products.name: SKILSAW SPT99-11 10 Inch Worm Drive Table Saw with Stand
products.description:
The SKILSAW SPT99-11 is a heavy-duty 10 inch table saw using worm drive gearing, with a 3-5/8 inch depth of cut, a 30-1/2 inch rip capacity, a rack and pinion fence and a rugged rolling stand with 16 inch wheels and load handles. Worm drive gearing is known for torque and durability, and the large wheels make it easy to roll across rough ground.

The tradeoff is weight and noise. Worm drive saws are heavier and louder than direct-drive designs, and the stand is large. Compared with the DEWALT DWE7491RS, the SKILSAW has a bit less rip capacity but more torque and a ruggedness aimed at framers and contractors. It suits tough jobsite use where the saw is moved over gravel and mud.

Check the gear oil level as directed, keep the fence rails clean and align the blade to the miter slot. Use sharp blades and let the motor cool after heavy use.
products.bestFor: Contractors who want a rugged, high-torque saw that rolls over rough ground.
pros: Worm drive gearing delivers torque for dense or wet lumber
Three and five-eighths inch depth of cut handles 4x stock in one pass
Sixteen inch wheels roll over gravel and rough ground
Rack and pinion fence stays accurate across the table
cons: Heavier and louder than direct-drive jobsite saws
Worm drive gearing needs periodic oil checks

products.name: SKIL TS6307 15 Amp 10 Inch Jobsite Table Saw with Folding Stand
products.description:
The SKIL TS6307 is a 10 inch jobsite saw with a 15 amp motor, rack and pinion fence rails, an integrated folding stand with legs that fold in for portability, and a micro-adjustment that lets you set the blade parallel to the rip fence and miter slot. It is aimed at homeowners and light contractors who want a 10 inch saw at an easy tier.

The tradeoff is refinement. The fold-in legs are lighter than a rolling stand but less stable and less convenient to roll, and the saw is a mid-tier build. Compared with the DEWALT DWE7491RS, the SKIL offers a similar blade size and rack and pinion fence, but lacks the rolling stand and the same fit and finish. It suits garage workshops where the saw is stored against a wall.

Check blade alignment after transport, keep the fence rails clean and use a push stick and riving knife. Fold the legs carefully and keep the pivot points free of dust.
products.bestFor: Home workshops that want a 10 inch saw with a folding stand at an easy tier.
pros: Ten inch blade handles typical 2x lumber and plywood
Rack and pinion fence rails keep the fence parallel
Integrated folding stand stores against a wall easily
Micro-adjustment makes blade alignment straightforward
cons: Folding legs are less stable than a rolling stand
Build and finish are less refined than premium models

products.name: DEWALT DWE7485 15 Amp 8-1/4 Inch Compact Jobsite Table Saw
products.description:
The DEWALT DWE7485 is a compact 8-1/4 inch jobsite table saw with a 15 amp motor, a 24.5 inch rip capacity that can handle half a sheet of plywood, rack and pinion telescoping fence rails and the Site-Pro modular guarding system that allows tool-free adjustments. It is smaller and lighter than 10 inch saws and is aimed at users who prize portability.

The tradeoff is capacity. An 8-1/4 inch blade cuts less deep than a 10 inch blade and a 24.5 inch rip needs more careful handling of full sheets. Compared with the DEWALT DWE7491RS, the 7485 is easier to carry and cheaper, but cuts thinner stock and has smaller tables. It suits trim carpenters, remodelers and anyone working in tight spaces.

Keep the guard clean and aligned, check the fence parallelism and use a push stick. Store it on a stand or bench when working.
products.bestFor: Trim carpenters and remodelers who need a light, easily carried saw.
pros: Compact size makes it easy to carry up stairs and into tight rooms
Site-Pro guarding adjusts without tools
Rack and pinion fence stays parallel and adjusts quickly
Twenty-four and a half inch rip handles half sheets of plywood
cons: Smaller blade limits depth of cut on thick lumber
Smaller table is less stable for large panels

products.name: Evolution R10TBLX 10 Inch Jobsite Table Saw with Wheeled Stand

specList.label: Included
specList.value: Zero-clearance throat plate and dado plate

products.description:
The Evolution R10TBLX is a 10 inch jobsite saw with a 15 amp soft-start motor, a rack and pinion fence, a zero-clearance throat plate, a dado plate for cutting grooves and a cross-cut sled in the box. Evolution markets its saws as multi-material cutters able to take specific blades for non-wood materials, and the included extras expand what the saw can do beyond ripping.

The tradeoff is that the extras do not replace core refinement. Compared with the DEWALT DWE7491RS, the Evolution comes with more accessories out of the box, but the fence, fit and finish are less proven. If you need dado cuts and crosscuts without buying add-ons, this is a good package. It suits hobbyists who want to try joinery and cross-cutting on a portable saw.

Check blade alignment, use the throat plate that matches your blade, and keep the stand wheels clean. Use the right blade for each material and never cut materials the manual does not allow.
products.bestFor: Hobbyists who want a dado plate and cross-cut sled included.
pros: Dado plate and zero-clearance throat plate expand cutting options
Cross-cut sled included for accurate crosscuts
Soft-start motor reduces the jolt on switch-on
Wheeled stand helps move the saw around a workshop
cons: Fence and finish are less proven than top-tier jobsite saws
Extras add little if you only rip lumber

buyingCriteria.explanation: Rip capacity is how far the fence can sit from the blade, and it decides whether you can rip a full sheet of plywood or only half. A 24.5 inch capacity, as on the DEWALT DWE7485, handles half sheets, while 30 to 32 inches handles most shelving and trim stock. Buy for the widest rip you do often.

The fence decides accuracy more than the motor. Rack and pinion fences, standard on all of these saws, move both ends together and stay parallel to the blade. Cheaper fences twist and lock out of square. Check fence parallelism before critical cuts.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Blade size and depth of cut
buyingCriteria.explanation: A 10 inch blade cuts about 3-1/8 to 3-5/8 inches deep, enough for 4x stock in two passes or one on a deep saw. An 8-1/4 inch blade, as on the DEWALT DWE7485 and SKIL TS6308, cuts about 2-1/2 inches. Choose by the thickest stock you cut.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Safety: guard, riving knife and brake
buyingCriteria.explanation: Table saws cause serious injuries, so guarding matters. Look for a riving knife that rises with the blade, a guard you can adjust without tools, and a brake, such as the Bosch convenience brake that stops the blade in about three seconds. Use push sticks and never reach over a spinning blade.

A rolling stand, as on the DEWALT 7491RS and SKILSAW SPT99, moves the saw easily on a site. Folding legs, as on the SKIL TS6307, store compactly but are less stable. A stand that rocks on uneven ground makes every cut less accurate.

A 15 amp motor is the limit for a standard household circuit and is common on all of these. Soft-start motors reduce the jolt. Cut quality depends more on the blade than the motor, so a good combination blade matters as much as the saw.

specDecoder.meaning: The maximum distance from the blade to the fence on the right side. It decides how wide a board you can rip.
specDecoder.watchFor: The DEWALT 7491RS lists 32-1/2 inches while the DEWALT 7485 and SKIL TS6308 list 24.5 inches.

specDecoder.meaning: The maximum blade height above the table at 90 degrees. It sets the thickest stock you can cut in one pass.
specDecoder.watchFor: The SKILSAW lists 3-5/8 inches, while the compact 8-1/4 inch saws list about 2-1/2 inches.

specDecoder.meaning: Amps show current draw and RPM shows blade speed. A 15 amp motor is the practical limit for a 120V circuit.
specDecoder.watchFor: The DEWALT 7491RS lists 4,800 RPM, while the Bosch GTS15-10 lists 3,800 RPM.

specDecoder.meaning: A gear-driven fence that moves both ends together so it stays parallel to the blade as you adjust.
specDecoder.watchFor: The SKIL TS6307 and the others in this guide list rack and pinion rails.

specDecoder.meaning: A system that stops the blade quickly after switch-off, reducing waiting time and some risk.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Bosch lists a brake that stops the blade in about three seconds.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and cut depth
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared rip capacity, blade size and depth of cut from published specifications. The DEWALT 7491RS leads on rip capacity, and the SKILSAW on depth. Compact saws were rated for lighter work.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fence and alignment
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at fence type and blade alignment features. All lineup saws use rack and pinion fences, and the SKIL TS6307 adds micro-adjustment. Fence accuracy was weighted heavily.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety features
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered guarding, riving knives and the Bosch blade brake. The DEWALT Site-Pro guarding earns credit for tool-free adjustment. We noted that no jobsite saw is a substitute for good technique.

howWeEvaluated.title: Stand and portability
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at stand type, wheels and weight, using owner feedback patterns on setup. The SKILSAW's large wheels and the Bosch Rise stand stood out. Folding legs were noted as lighter but less stable.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value and fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We matched each saw to a realistic user, from trim carpenter to deck builder. A bigger saw is not always better value. We judged by fit and what each extra feature adds.

cards.label: 10 inch
cards.text: A saw like the DEWALT 7491RS cuts deeper and rips wider, ideal for lumber, decks and shelving.

cards.label: 8-1/4 inch
cards.text: A saw like the DEWALT 7485 is lighter and easier to carry, ideal for trim and interior work.

howToChoose.note: Choose a 10 inch saw for lumber and an 8-1/4 inch saw if portability matters most.

rows: Sixteen inch wheels over rough ground

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A stable stand, a rack and pinion fence, a good riving knife and space for infeed and outfeed support. A saw you can store easily gets used more.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The SKIL TS6307 and DEWALT DWE7485 are easiest to store, and the Evolution adds a dado plate.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You rip daily or need a brake. The DEWALT 7491RS, Bosch and SKILSAW justify it.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You cut occasionally. The SKIL TS6307 is plenty.

maintenance.task: Check blade alignment to the miter slot
maintenance.why: A misaligned blade burns wood and increases kickback risk. A quick check with a square prevents both.
Dust jams rack and pinion rails and makes the fence stick. A dry lubricant keeps it smooth.
A dull blade burns, binds and strains the motor. A sharp blade is also safer.

maintenance.task: Clear dust from the motor housing
maintenance.why: Packed dust overheats the motor. Compressed air or a vacuum keeps vents clear.

maintenance.task: Inspect the riving knife and guard
maintenance.why: A bent knife or loose guard defeats their purpose. Realign or replace damaged parts.

faq.q: Is a 10 inch jobsite saw better than an 8-1/4 inch one?
faq.a: For lumber and sheet goods, yes, because it cuts deeper and rips wider. An 8-1/4 inch saw is lighter and easier to carry, which suits trim work.

faq.q: How much should I spend on a jobsite table saw?
faq.a: A basic 10 inch saw costs less, while a rolling-stand professional saw costs more. Spend for fence quality and stand, not just the motor.

faq.q: How long does a jobsite table saw last?
faq.a: A decent saw can last many years with care. Dust is the main enemy, so keep the motor and rails clean.

faq.q: Does a bigger motor mean a better cut?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Most jobsite saws use a 15 amp motor, and cut quality depends on the blade and the fence alignment.

Yes, they cause serious injuries. Use the guard, riving knife and push sticks, never reach across the blade and keep your body out of the line of kickback. Flesh-sensing saws exist at a much higher cost.

faq.q: Can I cut metal or plastic on a jobsite saw?
faq.a: Only if the manual and the blade allow it. Most saws are for wood, and cutting other materials needs the correct blade and settings.
